items.name: Iosevka
items.source_story_title: Iosevka is an open-source, sans-serif and slab-serif monospace font
items.summary: Customizable open-source monospace font, praised by a longtime user building personal variants.
items.why_included: A longtime user's enthusiastic endorsement explicitly highlights the custom-build system.
items.evidence: A user calls Iosevka their most-loved font for years and describes building a custom version.

evidence_sources.author: wartywhoa23
evidence_sources.excerpt: Iosevka, my absolutely most loved font for years! I've been using a custom version - you can customize the font¹ and build your own ttf (or better yet, ttc) using the build system supplied in the repository².

items.name: Proton Pass
items.summary: Password and passkey manager, praised for reliable use across a commenter's devices.
items.why_included: First-hand praise includes a concrete warning about accidentally mixing credential stores.
items.evidence: A user reports trouble-free use across their devices, but warns that saving passkeys into the wrong credential store can become annoying.

evidence_sources.author: teekert
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use ProtonPass on every device I own (religiously) and have never had an issue. But it's because I'm very careful to only deal with any credential ever via ProtonPass. I can imagine it gets annoying very fast if you accidentally put a passkey in the wrong place, ie because Chrome proposes it's own credentials store.

items.name: Sound — Bartosz Ciechanowski
items.summary: Interactive sound explainer progressing from bouncing air molecules to harmonics and interference.
items.why_included: Independent comment praise identifies the explainer's teaching progression rather than merely sharing its link.
items.evidence: A reader praises the progression from individual air molecules to understanding harmonics and interference.

evidence_sources.author: SwtCyber
evidence_sources.excerpt: The progression here is what impressed me most... You start with individual air molecules bouncing around and somehow end up understanding harmonics, interference and etc. Love this kind of articles!

evidence_sources.author: dofm
evidence_sources.excerpt: There is a wonderful Thames and Hudson book, Nature’s Palette, which includes Werner’s Nomenclature and expands on it by discussing how the nomenclature was produced, has illustrations of the reference plants and animals Werner used, etc.
